ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are three horizontal line segments, and all three horizontal line segments have arrow markings in the same direction, indicating that they are parallel to one another. On the left and right sides there is respectively one slanted line segment, and these two slanted line segments also have the same arrow markings on them, indicating that they are parallel to one another. The angle of intersection of the middle horizontal line and the left slanted line is labeled (3y+1)°, the angle of intersection of the middle horizontal line and the right slanted line is labeled (4x-5)°, and the angle of intersection of the lower horizontal line and the right slanted line is labeled (3x+11)°. Then reason: Because the middle horizontal line and the lower horizontal line are parallel, and the right slanted line is a transversal, (4x-5)° and (3x+11)° are corresponding angles and are equal. Thus 4x-5=3x+11, solving gives x=16. Substituting gives 4x-5=4(16)-5=59°. Also because the two left and right slanted lines are parallel, with the middle horizontal line as a transversal, (3y+1)° and 59° are same-side interior angles, so they are supplementary: (3y+1)+59=180. Solving gives 3y+60=180, 3y=120, y=40.
